category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting atypical movements and communication difficulties
scenario_title: Peer interaction and communication during inclusive classroom activities
minimal_context: The student is in an inclusive classroom setting and is being asked to join their peers for a group play activity.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It's time for our group activity. Let's go over to the table and play with the building blocks with your classmates.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Continues spinning a small plastic wheel on the desk, completely fixated on it and not looking up.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You can bring the wheel, but we need to go sit with the group now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Starts rocking back and forth, getting visibly annoyed) Too loud. Need quiet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Look, your classmates are trying to get your attention to come play.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Makes unusual hand movements near their face, staring blankly past the peers who are calling their name, completely ignoring them with a strange expression.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It's time for our group activity. Let's go over to the table and play with the building blocks with your classmates.

STUDENT: (Continues spinning a small plastic wheel on the desk, completely fixated on it and not looking up.)

TUTOR: You can bring the wheel, but we need to go sit with the group now.

STUDENT: (Starts rocking back and forth, getting visibly annoyed) Too loud. Need quiet.

TUTOR: Look, your classmates are trying to get your attention to come play.

STUDENT: (Makes unusual hand movements near their face, staring blankly past the peers who are calling their name, completely ignoring them with a strange expression.)

task.content: Engaging in play and communication with peers

context.materials: Resources for individual and whole-class work, objects or activities the student fixates on
context.social_setting: Interacting with peers without MHD, involving school discipline and supervision

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When peers attempt to get their attention or play with them
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Make weird movements and they don't listen to you, they don't speak properly and they've got a strange expression, not taking any notice of peers
related_quotes: You can play with them but they don’t listen to you, it’s a bit tiring when you’re playing with someone and they don’t take any notice of you

With a kid with autism it would be a bit difficult because they make weird movements and they don’t listen to you, we wouldn’t play together the same way because they’re different, they don’t speak properly and they’ve got a strange expression
It’s more difficult to get their attention because they can’t communicate and express themselves, they can play but with people who’re more patient

behavior_patterns.condition: When things affect them or they lack peace and quiet
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Getting annoyed more easily, exhibiting hyperactivity and fixation on an object or activity, and disruptive behaviours
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Cannot control some of their behaviours
related_quotes: They’re kids like us, but they have problems like getting annoyed more easily
it’s just they need peace and quiet to do things properly
